name: DEEPWELL NUMBERS: The Shelf Daily Draw
description: The oldest running numbers game on the Shelf, operated by a rotating coalition of Tier 1 bookmakers who change hands every quarter to avoid enforcement sweeps. Players pick a three-digit sequence tied to the day's synth-protein batch code, announced each morning at the distribution points. Payouts reach Φ800 on a Φ1 bet, and the house skims 22% — modest by underground standards — which has kept the operation trusted and alive for over two decades.
story_hooks: A bookmaker's runner discovers the batch codes are being manipulated upstream by someone inside HelixCorp's distribution network — the fix has been in for months, and the winners are not random.
A Tier 3 journalist embeds with a numbers operation to write an exposé but becomes financially and emotionally entangled when a grieving widow uses her last Φ5 and wins.
The rotating coalition's next handoff goes wrong when the outgoing bookmaker is found dead, and the new operator inherits both the ledger and whoever wanted the old one silenced.
